name: Mphasis Ltd
title: Mphasis Ltd - 526299 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Mphasis raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to low double digits on record pipeline (+23% YoY) and $466M net new TCV; cash conversion weak at 80% target.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered the strongest sequential constant-currency growth in three years, with Direct revenue up 3.5% QoQ and 11.3% YoY, broad-based across verticals and geographies. Net new TCV was $466M (six consecutive quarters above $400M), with TTM TCV at $1.8B and 66% of wins AI-led. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to low double digits from high single digits to low double digits, while keeping the EBIT margin band at 14.75%-15.75%. Cash flow was weak: OCF was $34M after normalizing for $39.5M of remittances delayed from 30 September to October, and DSO was 105 days normalized, with management guiding to double digits in Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Best sequential CC growth in three years
Mgmt says up about 10 days Q1 to Q2; expected to return to double digits in Q3

segments.name: Americas (Direct)
segments.commentary: Grew 3.1% QoQ and 12.4% YoY, driven by ramp-ups in large deal wins and new logos.

segments.name: Rest of World (Direct)
segments.commentary: Grew 16.4% QoQ and 23.5% YoY in constant currency, led by GCC participation with global clients.

segments.name: EMEA (Direct)
segments.commentary: Declined 3.3% QoQ and 9.0% YoY; management attributed this to a globally structured engagement allocated across regions, saying underlying health is intact.

segments.name: Enterprise Applications (APPS)
segments.commentary: 75.6% of revenue; Direct grew 3.7% QoQ and 14.4% YoY, driven by AI-led modernization deals.

segments.name: BPO
segments.commentary: Direct grew 6.6% QoQ and 18.7% YoY on new wins and AI-led propositions.

segments.name: ITO
segments.commentary: Declined 4.9% QoQ and 21.3% YoY as build-plus-run programs moved into run phase.

segments.name: BFS (Direct)
segments.commentary: Grew 4.5% QoQ and 15.0% YoY; eight-quarter CQGR of 3.8%.

segments.name: Insurance (Direct)
segments.commentary: Returned to sequential growth of 1.8% QoQ and grew 14.7% YoY; TTM growth 28%.

segments.name: TMT (Direct)
segments.commentary: Grew 10.9% QoQ and 14.5% YoY; TTM growth 12%. Now second-largest vertical after BFS.

segments.name: Logistics and Transportation
segments.commentary: Declined 12.0% QoQ on a smaller base, affected by geopolitical uncertainty; now under 4% of revenue.

segments.name: Others / Healthcare
segments.commentary: Others declined 6.4% QoQ and grew 1.8% YoY; Healthcare within it grew healthily and is expected to become a growth driver after a large deal win.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now expected in the low double digits, raised from high single digits to low double digits.
EBIT margin expected to stay stable within the 14.75%-15.75% target band while investing in capabilities; H1 at about 14.8%, with no split given between H1 and H2.
Operating cash flow conversion target of 80% of net income in FY27, normalizing further in FY28; management said FY28 should return to historic cash-generation levels.
Payments for acquired contracts expected to be lower in FY28 than FY27; Red Oak deal closing expected in November with a $28M commitment.
Furlough impact historically about 2% at organization level; no change expected this year, with mitigation work in December.
Expect large-deal TCV conversion to ramp in the next two to four quarters, though timing is lumpy.
capex_capacity: Investment continuing in Tria IP, coverage, sales and platforms; management expects to keep investing at least in the near term and does not see a maturity point yet.
Forward-deployed engineering (FDE) team capacity being expanded; value-stream offers packaged in Banking, Insurance and Healthcare.
Onsite mix rose sharply on AI programs, adding to margin pressure in the short term.
Tria platform launched in May 2026; first client deployments are live, and the company says it will share metrics over the next two quarters.
demand_pricing: Pipeline up 4.4% QoQ and 23% YoY to a record; AI-led share of pipeline rose to 71% from 12% at launch of Mphasis.ai three years ago; pipeline is now 3x its original size.
Opportunities below $20M grew 35% YoY and 9% QoQ; TCV for deals below $20M up 26% on a TTM basis.

Client demand is focused on AI engineering (harnesses, foundations), cyber hardening including post-quantum cryptography, and savings-led transformation combining vendor consolidation with operations transformation.
Top 5 clients grew 15.1% YoY (4.1% QoQ); Top 10 grew 13.0% YoY; Top 11-20 grew 22.7% YoY. Added two clients in the $50M+ bracket QoQ.

Management said the upgrade rests on backlog, pipeline and deal propensity, not on a jump in TCV; competition in outcome-based deals is intense and large players use balance sheets for deal structuring.

qa_highlights.question: Why upgrade guidance with TCV flat in the $400M range, and will pipeline convert to higher deal wins over the next 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Confidence comes from backlog, pipeline and client metrics; shape of TCV (short-cycle, +26% TTM) matters more than size. Large-deal TCV conversion is expected to ramp over the next two to four quarters, though timing is lumpy.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow: how will the H2 OCF-to-PAT ratio reach 80% given the delayed collections?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted DSO rose about 10 days Q1 to Q2 on a normalized basis and called it disappointing; recovery is expected to drive H2 cash improvement. No specific ratio was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the outcome-based revenue-share broker-dealer deal be sized, and how does its margin compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose sizing given competitive intensity, saying it is a percentage revenue share for a broker-dealer advisor network and could be bigger than estimated over five years; too early to call.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins behave on savings-led transformation deals?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO agreed the thesis holds: initial margins are lower and improve as platforms and automation mature, but a steady stream of new such deals will keep margins under pressure. Tailwind expected later, not necessarily in Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Logistics decline structural, comparable to DXC and mortgage?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO rejected the comparison: headwinds over five or six quarters, but the company is increasing investment in top accounts, with some clients top-two or top-three providers and potential for $20M accounts to grow to $50-100M.

qa_highlights.question: Cyber practice size and growth, and TMT sub-segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Cyber is not broken out; described as fast-growing and mainly in APPS. TMT sub-segments are device makers, telecom (rapid growth), hi-tech (small but growing) and ISVs (small).

risks_watch: Cash conversion: H2 needs a sharp recovery to hit the 80% OCF-to-PAT target; DSO must fall back to double digits in Q3.
Margin: H1 is at the low end of the band (around 14.8%); onsite mix shift, Tria amortization and investment could keep pressure on margins.
Large-deal conversion lumpiness; the TCV uplift the company expects has not yet shown up.
EMEA decline (-9.0% YoY) that management attributes to a cross-region allocation; to watch whether it reverses.
Logistics continues to shrink (-12% QoQ), and ITO is in a steep decline (-21.3% YoY).
Tria revenue and client adoption are undisclosed; management will share metrics over the next two quarters.
Outcome-based pricing competition and balance-sheet-funded deals from large peers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and guidance, citing backlog, pipeline and client metrics. Noticeably cautious and defensive on cash flow, calling the DSO and collection slippage disappointing, and evasive on Tria revenue metrics, margin split by half, and deal sizing.
key_quotes: Q2 delivered what we said it would: our strongest sequential growth in three years, broad-based across verticals and segments.
We now expect revenue growth in the low double digits for the full year.
Margins are something we can absolutely fix because that's more of an optimization exercise that can happen internally, but growth is really what is client dependent and that's where our focus is.
In a contractual business, forecasting revenues are always easier than forecasting cash flows.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided to low double digits (raised from high single to low double digits), backed by a record pipeline (+23% YoY), $466M net new TCV and 6 quarters above $400M, but no specific new capacity; management said the upgrade rests on backlog, pipeline and deal propensity rather than a TCV jump.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBIT margin about 14.8% in H1 at the low end of the 14.75%-15.75% band, with onsite mix shift and Tria amortization adding pressure; management only guides stable margins and says the tailwind comes later, not necessarily in Q3 or Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Forward-deployed engineering team capacity is being expanded and Tria is live, but no plant, line or headcount figure was given and capacity is not measured in utilisation terms.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pipeline is a record, up 23% YoY, net new TCV was $466M (six quarters above $400M) and Direct revenue grew 11.3% YoY, supporting FY27 low double-digit growth; large-deal conversion is lumpy.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not quantified; management says investment in Tria, coverage and platforms continues at least near term, but no capex amount or utilisation level was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth was just raised to low double digits, and management says the upgrade rests on backlog and pipeline, but TCV has not yet shown a jump and large-deal conversion is lumpy.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The 80% OCF-to-PAT target needs a sharp H2 recovery, DSO must fall from 105 days back to double digits in Q3, and EMEA is down 9.0% YoY and ITO down 21.3% YoY.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Tria platform launched in May 2026 with first client deployments live, and management says it will share metrics over the next two quarters; value-stream offers in Banking, Insurance and Healthcare are being packaged.

rows.label: DSO recovery and OCF conversion
rows.why: DSO rose about 10 days from Q1 to Q2 to 105 days normalized, and management guides to double digits in Q3 with $39.5M of delayed remittances now collected in October; the 80% OCF-to-net-income target for FY27 needs a sharp H2 recovery.

rows.label: Large-deal TCV conversion ramp
rows.why: Management expects large-deal TCV conversion to ramp over the next two to four quarters, but timing is lumpy and the TCV uplift has not yet shown up; Top 5 clients grew 15.1% YoY and two clients were added in the $50M+ bracket.

rows.label: Red Oak deal close and acquired-contract payments
rows.why: Red Oak deal closing is expected in November with a $28M commitment, and payments for acquired contracts are expected to be lower in FY28 than in FY27, which should help cash conversion.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, pipeline and the raised revenue guidance, but cautious and defensive on cash flow and DSO, and evasive on Tria metrics, the H1/H2 margin split and deal sizing; analysts pushed on TCV conversion, cash conversion and margin behaviour on savings-led deals.
